summary: The main article describes an electrochemical method for converting propargylic alcohols into trifluoromethylated allenes. It includes optimization tables, mechanistic schemes supported by DFT and kinetic studies, and a broad substrate scope including late-stage functionalization of pharmaceuticals.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: (A) Conventional allenylation of propargyl alcohol. (B) Electrochemical trifluoromethyl allenylation of propargyl alcohol.
items.description: Comparison between traditional two-electron nucleophilic substitution and the newly developed electrochemical radical pathway for allene synthesis.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction parameters. a,b a Reactions were conducted on 0.2 mmol scale. b Yields were determined by 19 F NMR spectroscopy using 2,2,2-tri fl uoroethanol as an internal standard.
items.description: This table details the optimization of reagents, solvents, electrodes, and current/potential settings for the trifluoromethylallenylation reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Evidence and implication of sodium cation assisted pre-association in electrochemical allenylation. (A) 1 H NMR titration experiment. (B) DFT calculations. (C) Differential pulse voltammetry. (D) Results of control experiments.
items.description: Experimental and computational evidence supporting the formation of a sodium-mediated complex between the alcohol and the trifluoromethyl source.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Mechanistic investigations. (A) Variations of 2b 's equivalent with standard condition. (B) Result of the divided cell experiment. (C) Computed relative free energies of transition state for concerted radical addition step. (D) Proposed mechanism based on mechanistic investigations.
items.description: Kinetic data and a proposed catalytic cycle showing the anodic oxidation and concerted radical addition steps leading to the allene product.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Substrate scope of electrochemical tri fl uoromethyl allenylation of propargyl alcohols. a,b a Reactions were conducted on 0.3 mmol scale. b Yields were determined by 19 F NMR using 2,2,2-tri fl uoroethanol as an internal standard. c Reactions were carried out under constant current condition. d Reactions were carried out under constant potential condition.
items.description: Demonstrates the broad applicability of the reaction across various aryl, heteroaryl, and complex drug-derived propargylic alcohols.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Synthetic utility of CF3-allenes.
items.description: Shows the downstream copper-catalyzed hydroboration of the synthesized trifluoromethyl allene to form an alkenyl boronate.
